one_line: Kerala temple-scholars of astronomy, mathematics and Sanskrit poetry in the late 16th–early 17th century.

appearance.age_look: Acyuta appears as a lean, late-50s scholar; Melpathur as a slightly younger, mid-40s poet, both with medium build and upright posture.
appearance.face: Warm brown complexions; Acyuta has an oval, slightly angular face with sharp nose, thin lips, narrow expressive eyes and a calm, analytical gaze; Melpathur has a softer rounder face with broader nose, fuller lips, large thoughtful eyes, and a serene, devotional half-smile.
appearance.hair: Both have thick, black hair with a few subtle greys; Acyuta’s is oiled and smoothly tied into a compact low bun at the nape with a neat central part and no headwear; Melpathur’s is similarly tied but slightly looser, with a gentle wave at the front and a red tilaka mark on his forehead.
appearance.costume: They wear late-medieval Kerala Brahmin temple-scholars’ dress: finely woven white cotton mundu (wrap-around dhoti) reaching to the ankles, pleated in front; an upper garment of soft off-white cotton angavastram draped over the left shoulder and across the chest, with Acyuta’s bordered by a thin dull-gold stripe and Melpathur’s by a slightly wider maroon stripe; both are bare-armed but modestly covered, with sacred thread diagonally across the torso; simple wooden bead mala around the neck, Acyuta also has a small palm-leaf manuscript cord tied at his left hip; feet in plain brown leather sandals; textiles are smooth, slightly off-white with subtle handloom texture, no fantasy patterns.
appearance.signature: Acyuta carries a bundled palm-leaf manuscript and a small wooden stylus, held like precise instruments of calculation; Melpathur carries a single, neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord, cradled with both hands as a treasured devotional text.

ref_desc: Acyuta and Melpathur are warm-brown Kerala scholars in white cotton mundu and angavastram with gold and maroon borders, compact low-bun black hair, sacred threads, bead malas, brown sandals, Acyuta holding palm-leaf manuscripts and stylus, Melpathur a red-tied palm-leaf scroll.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two late-16th-century Kerala temple-scholars standing side by side: Acyuta Pisharati lean and slightly older, Melpathur Narayana Bhattathiri softer and a bit younger. Both have warm brown complexions and black hair tied into compact low buns at the nape with a neat central part, Acyuta’s slightly more severe and Melpathur’s with a gentle wave at the front and a red tilaka on his forehead. Give Acyuta an oval, slightly angular face with sharp nose, thin lips, narrow eyes and a calm, analytical gaze; give Melpathur a rounder face with broader nose, fuller lips, large thoughtful eyes and a serene half-smile. Dress them in historically accurate Kerala Brahmin scholar clothing: white cotton mundu (dhoti) reaching the ankles, pleated in front, and off-white angavastram draped over the left shoulder and across the chest, Acyuta’s bordered with a thin dull-gold stripe and Melpathur’s with a wider maroon stripe. Show their sacred threads diagonally across the torso, simple wooden bead malas at the neck, and plain brown leather sandals. Acyuta’s left hip has a small cord securing extra palm-leaf strips. Place bundled palm-leaf manuscripts and a small wooden stylus in Acyuta’s hands, held like precise instruments, and a single rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord cradled reverently in Melpathur’s hands. Use a palette dominated by warm off-white, dull gold, maroon, and brown, and present them front-facing, full-body, with clear views of hair, faces, garments, jewellery, and props for consistent redrawing.
